public_payload.normalized_proposition: If hyperscalers stop AI spending, they will be judged on their AI returns, so they can't stop.
conditions: if they stop spending on AI

statement.excerpt: The problem that hyperscalers face is that they can’t really stop spending on AI, because once they do so, they’ll suddenly start getting graded on their AI investments.
statement.document_title: The More You Buy, The More You Lose

from_speaker: they can’t really stop spending on AI
they’ll suddenly start getting graded on their AI investments
our_interpretation: Treat this as a conditional prediction about investor scrutiny following a substantial halt or pullback in hyperscaler AI spending.
'Getting graded' means investors and analysts shift attention toward realized returns on previous AI investment.
The later context allows a substantial spending reduction rather than literal zero spending. Its suggested $15 billion threshold lacks a company and reporting period.
Continued spending alone cannot establish that fear of scrutiny caused it.
criteria.support_condition: A documented qualifying spending halt is followed by a clear shift toward evaluating realized AI returns, with evidence linking that shift to the halt.
criteria.contradiction_condition: After a documented qualifying halt and a meaningful investor reporting cycle, credible evidence shows that the predicted scrutiny shift did not occur. Existing scrutiny before a halt can challenge the 'suddenly start' wording but does not alone test the conditional outcome.
